title: The credentials must reach the SDK's auth, not its session
note: The refund seam built razorpay.Client POSITIONALLY while the SDK's signature is __init__(self, session=None, auth=None, **options), so the key id bound to session and the client called .post on a string. Every real refund raised AttributeError, which the seam's own handler converted into a RefundGatewayError and reported to the operator as 'the gateway declined'. The whole refund test class mocks razorpay.Client wholesale, so Client.__init__ never ran and a mock - which accepts any call shape - could not see the defect at all; the credential test actively pinned the positional form. M1 records the mutation that proves the replacement pin bites: with the keyword form reverted to positional, the un-mocked pin runs the REAL Client.__init__ and dies on the production symptom itself. Recorded because a pin that only ever runs against a mocked constructor cannot fail when the constructor is wrong.

mutations.description: the refund seam passes the credential pair to razorpay.Client positionally again, binding the key id to the SDK's `session` parameter instead of its `auth`
